task.description: You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0273-20260822 (already checked out and pushed by Step 00). Diagnose queue task 273 / ISS-0273 (GH#537): mix letflow.lint_handoffs' H6 check misclassifies test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs fixtures because pre_floor_file?/2 resolves @h6_floor_commit dynamically via `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` on every run (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex's h6_floor_commit/0 -> resolve_h6_floor_commit/0), rather than being pinned to a fixed commit sha. Step 0.5: check docs/issues/*.yaml for a prior resolved entry with matching symptoms -- ISS-0262 (see artifacts_in) is this exact mechanism's own origin and is the obvious candidate; determine whether this is a genuine NEW regression or a recurrence of a root cause ISS-0262 only partially closed (its own step-09-elixir-dev-implement-floor.json result.summary explicitly left @h6_floor_commit as a 'BOOTSTRAP placeholder ... for this implementation pass' and named an operational follow-up in the design doc's Section 2.3: whoever runs Step Final on that branch MUST edit the literal to the freshly-fetched origin/main tip sha before running post-rebase checks. Verify directly whether that follow-up step was ever actually done -- read the current value of @h6_floor_commit in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex (grep for it) and check git blame / git log on that line since the ISS-0262 merge (184d846, per `git log --oneline -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex`) to see if anyone ever pinned it. Step 1: reproduce directly -- run `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` on this branch right now and quote the actual failing output (which H6 assertions fail, and why -- trace exactly which fixture's git first-add commit is or isn't judged an ancestor of the currently-resolved floor). Trace root cause precisely: is @h6_floor_commit still literally the string "BOOTSTRAP" (i.e. never pinned, so it silently re-derives from a moving merge-base every single run, which is what the issue describes), or has main advanced past a real pinned value? State which. Then state a clear, reasoned recommendation: pin @h6_floor_commit to a fixed, specific commit sha (which one, and why that one specifically -- consider the commit that actually merged the H6 check onto main, 184d846, or its parent, whichever correctly marks the H6-feature boundary) and remove/simplify the runtime git-merge-base fallback path accordingly, OR some other fix if your investigation finds the root cause is different from what the issue report assumes. Do NOT implement the fix -- CODE-DESIGNER designs it from your diagnosis.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): docs/issues/ISS-0262.yaml is a clear match -- it is the exact same mechanism's origin (@h6_floor_commit / resolve_h6_floor_commit/0 / pre_floor_file?/2 in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex). This IS a recurrence, not a new independent defect: ISS-0262's implementation pass (rework_count 2) landed @h6_floor_commit as a documented 'BOOTSTRAP placeholder ONLY for this implementation pass' (see the comment block at lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:122-133) with an explicit operational follow-up in lib/letflow/design/iss0262-h6-floor-commit-addendum.md Section 2.3: 'whoever runs the next Step Final attempt on this branch MUST edit this literal to the freshly-fetched origin/main tip sha before running post-rebase checks.' That follow-up was never executed. Direct confirmation: `grep -n '@h6_floor_commit' lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` shows line 133 is still the literal `@h6_floor_commit "BOOTSTRAP"` today. `git blame -L 120,135 lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` attributes every line of that block, including line 133, to commit 184d846c ('fix: lint_handoffs detects non-JSON handoff files via new H6 check [WF03-ISS0262-20260822] (#525)') dated 2026-08-22 15:25:10 +0500 -- the commit that MERGED H6 onto main. No commit since 184d846 has ever touched that line (`git log --oneline -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` lists only eb680a5 (ISS-0191, built the task), 3288a76 (ISS-0190), and 184d846 (ISS-0262) -- nothing after). So the pin-the-literal step documented as mandatory was silently skipped when 184d846 was merged, and the mechanism has been running in its 'BOOTSTRAP' fallback mode (dynamic `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` re-resolution on every single invocation) on main ever since ISS-0262 closed. Per WF-03 Step 0.5, this recurrence should be flagged at least MAJOR (ISS-0262's own original severity) -- ISS-0273's queue entry currently has severity: MINOR, which undersells that this is the operational-follow-up gap the prior fix explicitly warned about, not a fresh cosmetic issue; flagging this in result.issues below for ORCH to reconsider.

STEP 1 (diagnose): Reproduced directly on this branch. `git fetch origin main -q && git merge-base HEAD origin/main` = 8e3a9644073fae9dc44cf61bdfcda2c798a0e01d (confirmed == `git rev-parse origin/main`, i.e. HEAD is currently a normal descendant of origin/main's tip). `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` result: 17/20 passed, 3 failed:

  1) T-NEW-AFTER-FLOOR-HARD-FAILS (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:297) -- `assert [violation] = result.hard_new` got `right: []` (left: `[violation]`)
  2) F-H6-CONTENT-NEVER-READ (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:127) -- `assert [%{rule: "H6"}] = result.hard_new` got `right: []`
  3) F-H6-FIRES-NEW (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:106) -- `assert [violation] = result.hard_new` got `right: []`

All three failures are the same root symptom viewed from three assertions: `LintHandoffs.lint_file(@fixture_file, @empty_schema)` (fixture = test/fixtures/lint_handoffs/h6/step-01-fixture-non-json.md, deliberately outside handoffs/ so production discovery never sees it, per design section 6.1) is called via the PRODUCTION path with no explicit floor argument, so it goes through `h6_floor_commit/0` -> `resolve_h6_floor_commit/0`. Because `@h6_floor_commit == "BOOTSTRAP"` (confirmed above), that function executes `System.cmd("git", ["merge-base", "HEAD", "origin/main"])` fresh on every test run, currently resolving to 8e3a9644... -- a commit far later than 184d846 (main has advanced substantially since ISS-0262 closed). `pre_floor_file?/2` then finds the fixture's first-add commit via `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%H --reverse -- <fixture>` and checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor <first_add_sha> <floor>`. I directly verified: `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%H --reverse -- test/fixtures/lint_handoffs/h6/step-01-fixture-non-json.md` = 184d846c... (the fixture was first added IN the same commit that merged H6), and 184d846c IS an ancestor of the current dynamic floor 8e3a9644 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 184d846 origin/main` -> exit 0). So `pre_floor_file?` now returns `true` for a fixture the test suite specifically designed to prove the 'added after the floor, must hard-fail' path -- it is misclassified as `hard_grandfathered` instead of `hard_new`. This is precisely the bug ISS-0273 describes: the floor is not a fixed point, so as origin/main keeps advancing, files that were correctly 'new' at H6-merge time silently slide into 'grandfathered' on every subsequent run, with zero code change to lint_handoffs.ex itself required to cause it -- pure environmental drift.

ROOT CAUSE (function-level): `resolve_h6_floor_commit/0` (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:197-212), reached because `@h6_floor_commit` (line 133) was never advanced past its documented BOOTSTRAP placeholder value when the branch that introduced it was merged. This is exactly the drift the design doc's own H6 rationale (moduledoc lines 38-46) was written to eliminate for handoff files, now reappearing one layer down in the mechanism meant to fix it.

RECOMMENDATION: Pin `@h6_floor_commit` to a fixed, specific sha and remove (or at minimum stop relying on) the runtime `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` fallback path in `resolve_h6_floor_commit/0`. The correct sha is 184d846's PARENT, c4a8e39729e253397d4f1aa34155a74522930252 -- NOT 184d846 itself. Reason, directly verified: the test fixture step-01-fixture-non-json.md was first added IN 184d846 (git log --follow --diff-filter=A shows its first-add sha == 184d846c), and `ancestor_or_equal?/2`'s `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <floor>` treats sha==floor as an ancestor (exit 0) -- so pinning to 184d846 itself would make the fixture pre-floor/grandfathered again, defeating the exact test (T-NEW-AFTER-FLOOR-HARD-FAILS, F-H6-FIRES-NEW, F-H6-CONTENT-NEVER-READ) that must prove the opposite. Pinning to the parent, c4a8e397, correctly places 184d846's own new content (H6 check code + its fixture + its design doc) on the 'new' side while keeping everything H6 was written to grandfather on the 'pre-floor' side -- verified directly: all 10 real WF03-ISS0258-20260822/*.md files' first-add commits (836a25bd423ec52a044463c5e8cb2b1f08554cb3, the ISS-0258 run) are ancestors of c4a8e397 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 836a25bd... c4a8e397` -> exit 0 for all 10, checked individually). This matches the task description's own framing ('184d846, or its parent, whichever correctly marks the H6-feature boundary') -- the parent is the one that actually works given the fixture's placement. CODE-DESIGNER should also decide, as part of the fix design, whether `resolve_h6_floor_commit/0`'s live git-merge-base fallback branch should be deleted entirely (since a pinned literal removes the only caller that needed it) or kept dormant as a documented fail-safe for a future BOOTSTRAP-style bootstrap -- I did not find a requirement either way in the existing design docs and am flagging it as an open design question rather than a diagnosed fact.
